School

Empiricism

Empiricism treats experience as the primary source of ideas and the test of knowledge claims about the world.

15 passages · 3 voices in this archive selection

Overview

British empiricists such as Locke, Berkeley, and Hume analyze how sensation and reflection generate ideas, and how far certainty extends. Empiricism shapes philosophy of science and everyday standards of evidence.

Historical notes

Early modern empiricism debates innate ideas and causation; later logical empiricism and contemporary naturalistic epistemology continue the lineage in new forms.

Core ideas

  • Ideas derive from experience.
  • Claims about the world require empirical credentials.
  • Skepticism about metaphysics beyond experience is a standing option.
  • Science exemplifies disciplined experiential inquiry.

Thinkers in this archive

John Locke , George Berkeley , David Hume

FAQ

What is empiricism?

It is the view that experience is the primary source of knowledge about the world.

Who are the main empiricists?

Locke, Berkeley, and Hume are the classic early modern figures.
